purpose: Record, append-only, the ODS-04 measurement of whether ODS v1's deterministic foundations and context layer produced real, evidenced efficiency gains without reducing rigor. This artifact is evidence about ODS v1; it does not modify docs/ops/ods/ODS_V1_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json and creates no new authority.
note_on_evaluated_state: This is the HEAD/TREE the ODS-04 prestate gate verified before measurement began (end of ODS-03). This evidence artifact is committed on top of it.

measurement_classes.MEASURED: Directly observed by running a command or counting bytes/lines in this session.
measurement_classes.DERIVED: An arithmetic or structural conclusion computed from two or more MEASURED values.
measurement_classes.QUALITATIVE: A judgment call without a numeric old-vs-new comparison, stated as such.

benchmark_a_prestate.old_pattern_observed_in_this_conversatio: ODS-00 and ODS-01 each ran one Bash call chaining `pwd && git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD && git rev-parse HEAD && git rev-parse HEAD^{tree} && git status --short`, then compared the four printed values against the prompt's expected values by reading — an LLM-mediated comparison with no hard exit code tied to a mismatch.
benchmark_a_prestate.new_pattern_measured: One command, `pnpm ods:prestate -- --branch <b> --head <sha> --tree <sha> --clean`, reproduced live in this session with exit 0 on match.
benchmark_a_prestate.llm_reasoning_required_new: NONE (machine PASS/FAIL exit code and per-field status)
benchmark_a_prestate.conclusion: Structural improvement: eliminated the possibility of a silently-wrong LLM-narrated match. Tool-call count is roughly unchanged (~1 call either way); what changed is that a mismatch can no longer pass unnoticed.

benchmark_b_authority_integrity.reconfirmation_method: Executed `NATIVE_RELATIONS.length` directly from the loaded module (23) after a naive `grep -c` first returned 24 — the extra match was the NativeRelation TYPE DECLARATION line, not a table entry. Recorded here as a reminder that this benchmark itself needed a negative-control-style correction.
benchmark_b_authority_integrity.manual_operations_replaced_per_run: Approximately 9 blob/content identity checks + 23 field-extraction-and-hash comparisons = 32+ discrete verification steps, each previously performed via ad hoc sha256sum/grep and narrated as matching across many prior certification rounds (see docs/ops/fib/FIB_IMPLEMENTATION_BASELINE_v1.0.0.wave1-closure.json and its predecessor audit chain).
benchmark_b_authority_integrity.reproducibility: Re-ran `pnpm authority:seal:verify` twice more in this session; both times AUTHORITY_SEAL_VERIFY=PASS in under 2 seconds wall clock.
benchmark_b_authority_integrity.negative_control_status: Operational — tests/ods/authority-seal-verify.test.ts exercises a 1-byte fixture mutation, a false native attestation, a stale recorded blob, a reduced/expanded corpus count, and a tampered ODS-authority input; all reproduced PASS in this session's full tests/ods/ run.
benchmark_b_authority_integrity.conclusion: Material improvement: 0 of these 32+ relationships had an executable check before ODS-C2; all 32+ now do.

benchmark_c_authority_context.reconciliation_with_ods_00_estimate: ODS-00 reported an approximate ~21:1 ratio using a chars/4 token proxy against the FIB index alone. This measurement uses actual byte counts across all three authorities' compact entry points and gets 89:1 (manifests) or 13.6:1 (FIB index alone) depending on which compact object is used as the comparison point. Per the ODS-04 instruction, this measured byte count supersedes the earlier approximation; both numbers are reported rather than silently picking the more favorable one.
benchmark_c_authority_context.conclusion: Material improvement: CLAUDE.md now codifies 'index/manifest first' as a mandatory retrieval order (section 3), and the measured compression is substantial under either compact-object definition.

benchmark_d_prompt.new_prompt_not_committed: The sample prompt was built and measured in the session scratchpad only, per the instruction not to embed pages of prompt copy here; only its metrics are recorded.
benchmark_d_prompt.old_prompt_comparison_reason: No exact pre-ODS Class B governed-implementation prompt exists as a machine-accessible repository artifact — prior governed rounds (e.g. the MSC-07B chain referenced in docs/ops/fib/FIB_IMPLEMENTATION_BASELINE_v1.0.0.wave1-closure.json) were conducted as conversation prompts never persisted to a file this session can read.
benchmark_d_prompt.qualitative_evidence: The recurring boilerplate this project's own ODS-01..ODS-04 prompts repeat each round — fail-closed rules, source-of-truth hierarchy, worktree/branch discipline, Windows hazards, report contract — is now the literal content of CLAUDE.md (96 lines) and the checkpoint standard (92 lines), directly observable by diffing those two documents' section headers against the repeated prose in this conversation's own ODS-01 through ODS-03 prompts.
benchmark_d_prompt.conclusion: The new-side measurement is real and demonstrates a materially small artifact is sufficient for a Class B task once CLAUDE.md/ODS-C6 exist. Rated conservatively (see scorecard) because no actual Wave 2 Class B task has yet been run under this regime to confirm the sample generalizes.

benchmark_e_poststate.verification_method: Loaded scripts/ods-poststate.ts directly and called composeSteps({allow:[],tests:[],requireClean:false}) in this session — returned exactly 3 steps, none named build or test:unit. Grepped the file for 'pnpm build'/'test:unit' — no match.
benchmark_e_poststate.aggregate_gate_role: CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) remains the merge-level aggregate: full typecheck, full test:unit (which already collects tests/ods/**), build, and the 7 generated-artefact verifiers all run there, not duplicated into ods:poststate.
benchmark_e_poststate.conclusion: Confirmed: ODS does not force a full suite/build for a small local task, and does not duplicate CI's aggregate work. Composition, not reimplementation, throughout.

benchmark_f_negative_control_value.class: MEASURED (from ODS-02/ODS-03 commit history in this same branch)

defects.description: A new untracked directory collapses to one `git status` summary line unless --untracked-files=all is passed, which would let an unauthorized file hide behind an allowed sibling.
defects.evidence: commit 2f705a2 (feat(ods): add deterministic scope gate) — fixed before that commit landed.

defects.description: `git mv` requires its destination directory to already exist; the rename-out-of-protected-surface test fixture omitted mkdirSync for it.
defects.classification: TOOL_ASSUMPTION_DEFECT (manifesting as a test-fixture setup bug — scripts/ods-scope.ts itself was never reached by the failing assertion)

defects.description: The ods-scope.test.ts real-CLI positive control hardcoded an allowlist snapshot that fell behind reality twice, once when scripts/ods-poststate.ts was added (ODS-02) and again when CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/the checkpoint standard/ci.yml were added (ODS-03) — ods-scope.ts itself was correct both times; the test's own fixture data was stale.

benchmark_f_negative_control_value.conclusion: All three were caught by running the validation battery before each commit, never after a false-green report to the operator. One (NC-1) was a real defect in a shipped gate; two (NC-2, NC-3) were defects in the verification apparatus itself — arguably the stronger result, since it shows the negative-control discipline also self-corrects its own test harness rather than only the code under test.

nc_3_recurred_live_during_this_measureme.observed: Running `pnpm exec vitest run tests/ods/` while drafting this very artifact reproduced NC-3 a fourth time: adding docs/ops/ods/ODS_V1_EFFICIENCY_VALIDATION_v1.0.0.json (an authorized ODS-04 file) made the same pre-existing ods-scope.test.ts positive control's hardcoded allowlist stale again, for the same structural reason as before.
nc_3_recurred_live_during_this_measureme.action_taken: NOT fixed here. ODS-04's authorized write surface restricts tests/ods/** to a genuine new regression test for a materially new defect discovered during measurement — this is neither: it is a known, already-cataloged TEST_FIXTURE_DEFECT (NC-3), not a new one, and scripts/ods-scope.ts itself is unaffected and correct.
nc_3_recurred_live_during_this_measureme.result: 78 of 79 tests/ods/** tests pass; the one failure is this known condition, reported honestly rather than silently fixed outside the authorized surface. Recommended follow-up: convert that one test's hardcoded allowlist to a base-relative pattern (or drop it in favor of the equivalent temp-repo coverage already present in the same file) the next time tests/ods/** is in an authorized write surface.
nc_3_recurred_live_during_this_measureme.significance: This is itself further Benchmark F evidence: the same defect class keeps resurfacing specifically because the discipline of running the full battery before every commit keeps re-detecting it — which is the point of the doctrine, not a sign it has failed.

read_only_findings_this_session.overhead_measurability_reason: No tool in this session can read the actual assembled system prompt or attribute token cost per plugin; the only path to a real measurement is a before/after A/B comparison, which requires mutating ~/.claude/settings.json.
read_only_findings_this_session.config_scope: ~/.claude/settings.json is user-level and shared across all of this operator's projects (68 sibling worktrees observed for unrelated Uellix workstreams alone) — a change here is not scoped to this repository.

ods_p1_plugin_decision.decision_reasoning: Expected benefit remains speculative (no measurement possible without mutation), the only measurement path mutates shared user-level configuration used by unrelated work, and it is not on the critical path to Wave 2. This satisfies the ODS-04 decision standard's explicit preference for DEFER under these exact conditions, and closes the v1 treatment of ODS-P1 as PILOT (not ADOPT_NOW) without blocking ODS_V1_OPERATIONAL.

rating_notes.PROMPT_EFFICIENCY: Not rated MATERIAL: the new-side measurement is real (608 bytes/15 lines) but no numeric old-side comparison exists, and no actual Wave 2 Class B task has run under this regime yet to confirm the sample generalizes.
rating_notes.CLASS_B_ROUTING: Not rated MATERIAL: adjudicated VALIDATED with an honest evidentiary caveat (repository-outcome + session record, not cryptographic model-identity proof); rated MODEST here to avoid overclaiming on the same scale used for hard measurements.
rating_notes.OPERATOR_COPY_PASTE_REDUCTION: Governed commands replaced multi-step manual verification sequences, but Class A prompts in this very conversation remain long by design (appropriate for their routing class) — the reduction is real but partial.

unresolved_limitations: No real Wave 2 Class B task has been executed under ODS v1 yet — Benchmark D and the CLASS_B_ROUTING rating rely on a constructed representative example and two process/foundation-building rounds (ODS-02, ODS-03), not a product implementation round.
Plugin/session startup overhead (T1) remains unmeasured and unresolved by design (ODS-P1 DEFER) — it is not blocking, but it is not closed as an efficiency gain either.
PROMPT_EFFICIENCY and OPERATOR_COPY_PASTE_REDUCTION have no numeric pre-ODS baseline; both ratings are conservative for exactly this reason.

This artifact's own benchmark B relied on the same authority-seal-verify.ts logic it is evaluating — mitigated by independently re-deriving the 23-relation count from the loaded module rather than trusting a prior claim, and by re-running the full negative-control suite live in this session rather than citing past results only.

78 of 79 tests/ods/** tests pass as of this commit — the one failure is a live fourth recurrence of the already-documented NC-3 test-fixture staleness (see benchmark_f_negative_control_value.nc_3_recurred_live_during_this_measurement), left unfixed because ODS-04's authorized write surface does not extend to it. scripts/ods-scope.ts itself is correct and unaffected.
